text.text_excerpt: We didn't hang out on Bourbon Street too much, but if I had to spend more time anywhere along that stretch, it would be here. I LOVE a dueling piano bar, especially one with no cover (take that, Nashville) and some of the guys here were fantastic! One guy was blind, and we were duly super-impressed with his awesome Stevie Wonder abilities. Lots of fun drunk people dancing around in front of the piano, great songs to sing along too, and they take requests! Just drop $5 minimum in the jar and ask for it, they'll give you a shout out. Not the classiest of places, but you're on Bourbon Street, and this is one of the most fun places we saw. Not too crazy crowded or full of disgusting gross wei...

Judge me all you want, but I had a really good time here. This is a cute little piano bar that does a good job of getting the crowd going. We stopped in here after the Yelp awards looking for some good music and to have fun. There was a "washboard" player who pulled me on stage so I could dance around like a dope and play his washboard. They play a lot of classic piano type songs like Billy Joel and some music you can dance to as well. I know that this place is more of a tourist hang, but I had a blast here and I wouldn't hesitate to return if I was in the mood for something a little bit different. I almost prefer it over Pat O's piano bar because this spot encourages dancing.

From all the piano bars on Bourbon street I feel like the most talented of piano players are here. Pretty legit skills. Drinks were made good and quick. Good bartender service. The set up of the bar could be a little bit better to accommodate a larger crowd. Good prices on drinks. Pretty solid experience here.
